title: populus × canadensis var. gelrica
intro: Populus × canadensis var. gelrica, commonly known as Black Cottonwood, is a hybrid deciduous tree native to North America, known for its distinctive heart-shaped leaves and robust growth. The bark of the Black Cottonwood tree contains bioactive compounds that have been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including fever reduction, pain relief, and digestive problems. The therapeutic actions of Black Cottonwood are attributed to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which can help to soothe skin irritations and reduce swelling. The bioactive constituents of Black Cottonwood include salicin, a compound similar to aspirin, which contributes to its analgesic and antipyretic effects.
